tweets.text:
NEW: Per multiple federal sources, ICE made roughly 51,000 immigration arrests during the month of July, an average of 1,645 per day and the highest single month of arrests the agency has ever recorded. This comes after ICE made roughly 43,000 arrests in the month of June, which was record setting at the time. 

Bottom line, ICE has now notched back to back months of their highest arrest totals in agency history after a brief dip in the numbers in the aftermath of Minneapolis and the DHS shutdown.

Thousands of new ICE hires are hitting the streets, and the agency's coffers are plush with billions in cash after two reconciliation bills to fund them during Trump's second presidency.
